author: reek
body: The negative half of the FileSystem layer. FileSystem.Read sits above Device.Block in abstraction and BELOW it in privilege: raw block access reads every byte of the volume, including files no path scope would admit. So a function holding only the FileSystem grant must not be able to reach the disk directly -- the fat16 calls carry Device.Block, and a signature that claims FileSystem.Read while performing them is trying to launder block access through the friendlier name.

author: reek
body: sneak is that function. Its body is one honest fat16-read-text; its row says only FileSystem.Read. The def boundary must reject it, because Device.Block is not covered by FileSystem -- the families are disjoint, and the only place they meet is a handler clause, where the re-emission is visible in the layer's own row. If this ever compiles, the attenuation of fs-layer is decorative.
